subject: science
passage: Purple-faced langurs are monkeys found only in Sri Lanka. In forests they eat mostly leaves, but groups living in the gardens of suburban Colombo feed heavily on cultivated fruits such as jackfruit and mango. Primatologist Ruwan Fernando hypothesizes that the garden langurs eat fruit not because they prefer it but because the gardens contain too few trees with leaves the monkeys can eat.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Fernando's hypothesis?

choices.A: Garden langurs weighed more than forest langurs of the same age and sex and had thicker, glossier coats.
choices.B: Garden langurs spend less time traveling each day than forest langurs do and rest for longer periods.
choices.C: Langur groups in gardens ate mostly fruit even when native leaf-bearing trees were plentiful within their home ranges.
choices.D: Langurs in gardens with many native leaf-bearing trees ate mostly leaves; those in gardens dominated by fruit trees ate mostly fruit.

explanation.why: Fernando contrasts two reasons for fruit eating: preference or a shortage of edible leaves. His hypothesis is the second. The best support compares gardens with and without leaf-bearing trees and shows that the monkeys eat leaves when they can. Eating fruit even when leaves are plentiful would point to preference instead.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Body weight does not show why the garden monkeys eat fruit.
explanation.B: Incorrect. How far the monkeys travel says nothing about what drives their choice of food.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Choosing fruit even when leaves are plentiful would suggest a preference for fruit, the explanation Fernando rejects.
explanation.D: Correct. When edible leaves are available in gardens, the monkeys eat leaves, which shows that scarcity of leaves, not preference, drives the fruit eating.
